cards.front: How does nephritic syndrome differ from nephrotic syndrome?
cards.back: **Nephritic**: glomerular inflammation; **hematuria with RBC casts**, **hypertension**, oliguria, rising creatinine, and proteinuria usually below the nephrotic range. **Nephrotic**: podocyte or GBM damage; **heavy proteinuria** (>3.5 g/day), hypoalbuminemia, **edema** and hyperlipidemia.
cards.back_pt: **Nefrítica**: inflamação glomerular; **hematúria com cilindros hemáticos**, **hipertensão**, oligúria, aumento da creatinina e proteinúria geralmente abaixo da faixa nefrótica. **Nefrótica**: lesão do podócito ou da MBG; **proteinúria maciça** (>3,5 g/dia), hipoalbuminemia, **edema** e hiperlipidemia.

cards.front: Why are patients with nephrotic syndrome at risk of thrombosis and infection?
cards.back: **Thrombosis**: urinary loss of **antithrombin III** (and other anticoagulant proteins) plus higher hepatic clotting factor synthesis; **renal vein thrombosis** is classic. **Infection**: urinary loss of **IgG** and complement; higher risk of infection by encapsulated bacteria such as *S. pneumoniae* (e.g., spontaneous peritonitis).
cards.back_pt: **Trombose**: perda urinária de **antitrombina III** (e de outras proteínas anticoagulantes) e maior síntese hepática de fatores de coagulação; a **trombose de veia renal** é clássica. **Infecção**: perda urinária de **IgG** e complemento; maior risco de infecção por bactérias encapsuladas, como *S. pneumoniae* (ex.: peritonite espontânea).

cards.front: What are the immune mechanism and biopsy findings of post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis?
cards.back: **Type III hypersensitivity** (immune complexes). **Low C3**. IF: granular, **lumpy-bumpy** IgG and C3. EM: **subepithelial humps**. LM: enlarged, hypercellular glomeruli with neutrophils.
cards.back_pt: **Hipersensibilidade tipo III** (imunocomplexos). **C3 baixo**. IF: depósitos granulares de IgG e C3, aspecto *lumpy-bumpy*. ME: **corcovas subepiteliais** (*humps*). MO: glomérulos aumentados e hipercelulares, com neutrófilos.

cards.front: How does the timing of hematuria after an infection separate IgA nephropathy from post-streptococcal GN?
cards.back: **IgA nephropathy** (Berger): hematuria **within 1-3 days** of a URI or GI infection; **mesangial IgA** on IF; normal complement. **PSGN**: hematuria about **2-3 weeks** after pharyngitis (longer after skin infection); low C3.
cards.back_pt: **Nefropatia por IgA** (doença de Berger): hematúria **em 1-3 dias** após infecção de vias aéreas superiores ou gastrointestinal; **IgA mesangial** na IF; complemento normal. **GN pós-estreptocócica (GNPE)**: hematúria cerca de **2-3 semanas** após faringite (mais tarde após infecção de pele); C3 baixo.

cards.front: Which ANCA pattern goes with each pauci-immune crescentic GN?
cards.back: **Granulomatosis with polyangiitis**: **c-ANCA (anti-PR3)**; sinus, lung and kidney. **Microscopic polyangiitis**: **p-ANCA (anti-MPO)**; no granulomas. **Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA)**: **p-ANCA (anti-MPO)**; asthma and eosinophilia. **Pauci-immune**: little or no staining on IF.
cards.back_pt: **Granulomatose com poliangiite**: **c-ANCA (anti-PR3)**; seios da face, pulmão e rim. **Poliangiite microscópica**: **p-ANCA (anti-MPO)**; sem granulomas. **Granulomatose eosinofílica com poliangiite**: **p-ANCA (anti-MPO)**; asma e eosinofilia. **Pauci-imune**: pouca ou nenhuma marcação na IF.

cards.front: What causes Alport syndrome, and what are its three classic findings?
cards.back: Defective **type IV collagen**, most often **X-linked** (alpha-5 chain), so the GBM becomes **thin**, then thick and **split** (*basket-weave* on EM). Findings: **hematuria** progressing to renal failure, **sensorineural hearing loss**, and **eye problems** (e.g., anterior lenticonus).
cards.back_pt: Defeito do **colágeno tipo IV**, mais frequentemente **ligado ao X** (cadeia alfa-5), com MBG inicialmente **fina** e depois espessada e **fragmentada** (aspecto em *cesta de vime*/*basket-weave* na ME). Achados: **hematúria** com progressão para insuficiência renal, **perda auditiva neurossensorial** e **alterações oculares** (ex.: lenticone anterior).

cards.front: What is focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), and what conditions are linked to it?
cards.back: Nephrotic syndrome with **sclerosis of part of some glomeruli** and foot process effacement on EM. Links: **HIV** (collapsing type), **heroin**, **obesity**, sickle cell disease. It responds to steroids **less well** than minimal change disease.
cards.back_pt: Síndrome nefrótica com **esclerose de parte de alguns glomérulos** e apagamento dos pedicelos na ME. Associações: **HIV** (forma colapsante), **heroína**, **obesidade**, doença falciforme. Responde **pior** aos corticoides do que a doença de lesões mínimas.

cards.front: What are the glomerular findings in diabetic nephropathy, and why do ACE inhibitors or ARBs help?
cards.back: **Nonenzymatic glycation** thickens the **GBM** and expands the mesangium; nodular sclerosis forms **Kimmelstiel-Wilson nodules**. **ACE inhibitors and ARBs** block angiotensin II constriction of the **efferent arteriole**, lower intraglomerular pressure, reduce proteinuria and slow progression.
cards.back_pt: A **glicação não enzimática** espessa a **MBG** e expande o mesângio; a esclerose nodular forma os **nódulos de Kimmelstiel-Wilson**. **IECA/BRA** bloqueiam a vasoconstrição da **arteríola eferente** pela angiotensina II, reduzem a pressão intraglomerular, diminuem a proteinúria e retardam a progressão.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man who smokes has coughed up blood for 1 week. For 3 days his urine has been dark. Blood pressure is 152/94 mm Hg. Chest x-ray shows patchy bilateral alveolar opacities. Serum creatinine is 3.6 mg/dL; it was 0.9 mg/dL 2 months ago. Urinalysis shows red blood cell casts and 2+ protein. Renal biopsy shows crescents in most glomeruli. Immunofluorescence shows a smooth linear pattern of IgG along the glomerular basement membrane. Against which antigen are this patient's antibodies most likely directed?
choices: Alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen
questions.explanation: Lung hemorrhage, rapidly progressive GN with crescents, and **linear IgG** on IF define **Goodpasture syndrome** (anti-GBM disease). The antibodies bind the **alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen** in glomerular and alveolar basement membranes (type II hypersensitivity). Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (anti-PR3) also causes lung and kidney disease, but its GN is **pauci-immune**, with little or no IF staining.
questions.explanation_pt: Hemorragia pulmonar, GNRP com crescentes e **IgG linear** na IF definem a **síndrome de Goodpasture** (doença anti-MBG). Os anticorpos se ligam à **cadeia alfa-3 do colágeno tipo IV** das membranas basais glomerular e alveolar (hipersensibilidade tipo II). A granulomatose com poliangiite (anti-PR3) também acomete pulmão e rim, mas sua GN é **pauci-imune**, com pouca ou nenhuma marcação na IF.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man was diagnosed with Hodgkin lymphoma 1 month ago and has not yet started treatment. He now has swelling of his face and legs. Blood pressure is 118/74 mm Hg. Urinalysis shows 4+ protein, no red blood cells and oval fat bodies. Serum albumin is 1.9 g/dL, total cholesterol is high, and creatinine is normal. Renal biopsy shows normal glomeruli on light microscopy and a Congo red stain is negative. Immunofluorescence is negative. Electron microscopy shows diffuse effacement of podocyte foot processes and no deposits. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Nephrotic syndrome with **normal glomeruli on light microscopy**, negative IF and **diffuse foot process effacement** on EM is **minimal change disease**, a known association of **Hodgkin lymphoma**. FSGS also shows foot process effacement on EM, but light microscopy shows **segmental sclerosis**. Amyloidosis would show Congo red-positive deposits with apple-green birefringence.
questions.explanation_pt: Síndrome nefrótica com **glomérulos normais à microscopia óptica**, IF negativa e **apagamento difuso dos pedicelos** na ME é **doença de lesões mínimas**, associação conhecida do **linfoma de Hodgkin**. A GESF também mostra apagamento dos pedicelos na ME, mas a microscopia óptica mostra **esclerose segmentar**. A amiloidose mostraria depósitos positivos ao vermelho Congo, com birrefringência verde-maçã.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man has had progressive leg swelling for 2 months. He takes no medications. Blood pressure is 128/80 mm Hg. Urinalysis shows 4+ protein and no red blood cell casts. Serum albumin is 2.2 g/dL. ANA, hepatitis B and hepatitis C tests are negative, and age-appropriate cancer screening is normal. Renal biopsy shows diffusely thickened capillary walls without hypercellularity. A silver stain shows spikes along the glomerular basement membrane. Immunofluorescence shows granular IgG and C3, and electron microscopy shows subepithelial deposits. Which serum antibody is most likely present?
questions.explanation: An adult with nephrotic syndrome, a thick GBM with **spikes** and **subepithelial deposits** has **membranous nephropathy**. With no secondary cause found, this is primary disease, which is usually caused by **anti-PLA2R** antibodies against a podocyte antigen. Lupus can cause membranous nephropathy (class V), but a negative ANA makes anti-dsDNA very unlikely.
questions.explanation_pt: Um adulto com síndrome nefrótica, MBG espessada com **espículas** (*spikes*) e **depósitos subepiteliais** tem **nefropatia membranosa**. Sem causa secundária identificada, trata-se da forma primária, que geralmente é causada por anticorpos **anti-PLA2R** contra um antígeno do podócito. O lúpus pode causar nefropatia membranosa (classe V), mas um FAN negativo torna o anti-DNA nativo (anti-dsDNA) muito improvável.

questions.stem: A 49-year-old woman with chronic hepatitis C has had joint pain and a purple, raised rash on her legs for 1 month. She now has leg edema. Blood pressure is 158/96 mm Hg. Urinalysis shows 3+ protein, red blood cells and red blood cell casts. Serum cryoglobulins are present, and C3 and C4 are low. Renal biopsy shows hypercellular glomeruli with a double-contoured, split-looking basement membrane on silver stain. Electron microscopy shows subendothelial deposits. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Hepatitis C with **cryoglobulinemia**, low complement, a **tram-track** (split) GBM and **subendothelial deposits** points to **membranoproliferative GN**, which can present with mixed nephritic and nephrotic features. Membranous nephropathy is also linked to viral hepatitis, but it has **subepithelial** deposits, a thick GBM with spikes and no hypercellularity, and red blood cell casts are not typical. Purpura, joint pain and nephritis can also suggest IgA vasculitis, but IgA disease has **normal complement** and **mesangial** IgA deposits, not cryoglobulins.
questions.explanation_pt: Hepatite C com **crioglobulinemia**, complemento baixo, MBG em **trilho de trem** (*tram-track*, duplicada) e **depósitos subendoteliais** indicam **GN membranoproliferativa**, que pode se apresentar com quadro misto nefrítico e nefrótico. A nefropatia membranosa também se associa a hepatites virais, mas tem depósitos **subepiteliais**, MBG espessada com espículas e sem hipercelularidade, e cilindros hemáticos não são típicos. Púrpura, artralgia e nefrite também podem sugerir vasculite por IgA, mas a doença por IgA tem **complemento normal** e depósitos **mesangiais** de IgA, sem crioglobulinas.

notes.title: Glomerular disease: nephritic and nephrotic patterns
notes.body_md:
## Two patterns

- **Nephritic**: inflammation; **hematuria with RBC casts**, hypertension, oliguria, azotemia, modest proteinuria.
- **Nephrotic**: **proteinuria >3.5 g/day**, hypoalbuminemia, edema, **hyperlipidemia** with fatty casts.
- Nephrotic risks: **thrombosis** (loss of antithrombin III; renal vein thrombosis) and **infection** (loss of IgG).

## Nephritic causes

- **Post-streptococcal GN**: children, 2-3 weeks after pharyngitis or later after skin infection; **low C3**; granular *lumpy-bumpy* IF; **subepithelial humps**.
- **IgA nephropathy** (Berger): hematuria **1-3 days** after a URI; **mesangial IgA**; normal complement.
- **Alport syndrome**: usually X-linked **type IV collagen** defect; hematuria, **hearing loss**, eye findings.

## Rapidly progressive GN (crescents)

- **Goodpasture**: anti-GBM antibodies to the **alpha-3 chain of type IV collagen**; **linear IgG**; lung hemorrhage.
- **Pauci-immune** (ANCA): **GPA** (c-ANCA, PR3), **microscopic polyangiitis** and **eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis** (EGPA) (p-ANCA, MPO).
- **Granular** immune-complex crescentic GN: severe PSGN or lupus.

## Nephrotic causes

- **Minimal change disease**: children; normal LM; **foot process effacement** on EM; selective albuminuria; responds to steroids; linked to recent infection, NSAIDs, **Hodgkin lymphoma**.
- **FSGS**: segmental sclerosis; **HIV**, heroin, obesity, sickle cell; poorer steroid response.
- **Membranous nephropathy**: adults; thick GBM, **spike and dome**, subepithelial deposits; primary form with **anti-PLA2R**; secondary to hepatitis B, drugs, solid tumors, SLE.
- **Diabetic nephropathy**: GBM thickening, **Kimmelstiel-Wilson nodules**; ACE inhibitors or ARBs slow progression.
- **Amyloidosis**: **Congo red**, apple-green birefringence under polarized light.

## Mixed pictures

- **MPGN**: **tram-track** GBM; hepatitis C and **cryoglobulinemia**; low complement.
- **Lupus nephritis**: classes I-VI; **diffuse proliferative** (class IV) is the most common and most severe, with *wire loops*; class V is membranous; **full-house** IF.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Dois padrões

- **Nefrítico**: inflamação; **hematúria com cilindros hemáticos**, hipertensão, oligúria, azotemia, proteinúria moderada.
- **Nefrótico**: **proteinúria >3,5 g/dia**, hipoalbuminemia, edema, **hiperlipidemia** com cilindros graxos.
- Riscos no nefrótico: **trombose** (perda de antitrombina III; trombose de veia renal) e **infecção** (perda de IgG).

## Causas nefríticas

- **GN pós-estreptocócica**: crianças, 2-3 semanas após faringite ou mais tarde após infecção de pele; **C3 baixo**; IF granular *lumpy-bumpy*; **corcovas subepiteliais**.
- **Nefropatia por IgA** (doença de Berger): hematúria **1-3 dias** após infecção de vias aéreas superiores; **IgA mesangial**; complemento normal.
- **Síndrome de Alport**: defeito do **colágeno tipo IV**, geralmente ligado ao X; hematúria, **perda auditiva**, alterações oculares.

## GN rapidamente progressiva (crescentes)

- **Goodpasture**: anticorpos anti-MBG contra a **cadeia alfa-3 do colágeno tipo IV**; **IgG linear**; hemorragia pulmonar.
- **Pauci-imune** (ANCA): **GPA** (c-ANCA, PR3), **poliangiite microscópica** e **granulomatose eosinofílica com poliangiite** (GEPA) (p-ANCA, MPO).
- GN crescêntica por imunocomplexos (IF **granular**): GNPE grave ou lúpus.

## Causas nefróticas

- **Doença de lesões mínimas**: crianças; MO normal; **apagamento dos pedicelos** na ME; albuminúria seletiva; responde a corticoides; associada a infecção recente, AINEs, **linfoma de Hodgkin**.
- **GESF**: esclerose segmentar; **HIV**, heroína, obesidade, doença falciforme; pior resposta aos corticoides.
- **Nefropatia membranosa**: adultos; MBG espessada, padrão *spike and dome*, depósitos subepiteliais; forma primária com **anti-PLA2R**; secundária a hepatite B, medicamentos, tumores sólidos, LES.
- **Nefropatia diabética**: espessamento da MBG, **nódulos de Kimmelstiel-Wilson**; IECA ou BRA retardam a progressão.
- **Amiloidose**: **vermelho Congo**, birrefringência verde-maçã à luz polarizada.

## Quadros mistos

- **GNMP**: MBG em **trilho de trem** (*tram-track*); hepatite C e **crioglobulinemia**; complemento baixo.
- **Nefrite lúpica**: classes I-VI; a **proliferativa difusa** (classe IV) é a mais comum e a mais grave, com alças em *wire loop*; a classe V é membranosa; IF *full-house*.
